blockers: Phase 2d (editor UI + XP-cost rules + rules/creator/migration test coverage): Sidereal now has a real editor UI branch in Exalted1eEditor.tsx (a Caste <select> sourced from siderealCastes, its own Charms & Sorcery catalog with a Caste filter using Sidereal's own five Castes instead of Abyssal's, its shared-catalog Merits/Flaws subset via siderealOnlyTraits with Sidereal's own cost caps enforced in the UI, and its 12-entry Backgrounds list), a new getSiderealPowerExperienceCost/isSiderealAbilityFavored XP-cost function pair in shared/advancement/rules.ts (favored-Auspicious-Ability/favored-Ability discount, mirroring Abyssal's Phase 1e pattern but keyed to Sidereal's own siderealAbilityGroups in definitions.ts, which was derived directly from the promoted Charm catalog's own caste/ability fields rather than guessed), and new test coverage across exalted-shared-records.test.ts (XP-cost rules), exalted-creation-panel.test.tsx (guided-creation UI, a new 'ExaltedCreationPanel (Sidereal guided creation, Phase 2d)' describe block), sidereal-powers-editor.test.tsx (new file: Charms/Sorcery catalog browsing, Caste filtering, and the XP-learn flow end to end), and exalted1e-sidereal.test.ts (a new 'Schema migration (Phase 2d: migration-dimension coverage)' describe block). rulesTests/creatorTests/migrationTests all now pass as a result.

Phase: Astrology/Colleges closed the catalog dimension. The previous blocker's '5 of 365 promotable rows' estimate undercounted -- a precise recount against the full inventory found exactly 10 unpromoted disposition-calculated Astrology/Resplendent-Destinies rows (sidereal-astrology-petitions, -effect-roll, -blessings-and-curses, -scope-duration-power, -multiple-and-canceling-effects, -censure, -paradox, -pattern-bite, -greater-signs, and resplendent-destinies), not 5. All 10 are now promoted verbatim (id-matched to their inventory row, per auditPromotedCatalog's rule) into a new sidereal-astrology-rules.json catalog file. promotableEntries was corrected from 365 to 370 (+5, replacing the old approximate Astrology count with the precise one) and promotedEntries increased from 360 to 370 (+10 newly promoted), so catalogDimensionPasses' promotedEntries === promotableEntries check now holds (370 === 370), alongside unresolvedEntries === 0 and a non-empty checksum -- catalogDimensionPasses now returns true for Sidereal. catalog.checksum is scripts/audit-exalted-sources.mjs's real computed value (b733726d), an FNV-1a hash over the id-sorted entries of every sidereal-*.json file (sidereal-charms.json's 193 Charms plus sidereal-astrology-rules.json's 10 new rules rows = 203 file-glob-scoped entries; see exalted1e-source-audit.test.ts for why this differs from catalog.promotedEntries above). A separate, richer reference catalog (sidereal-astrology.ts: 5 Houses, 25 named Colleges each mapped 1:1 to Sidereal's own siderealAbilityGroups, ~75 named Resplendent Effects, 5 Greater Signs, 8 generic Blessing/Curse types) was also built and wired into a new SiderealAstrologyPanel.tsx (College dot-ratings, a Resplendent Destinies manager linked to schema.ts's new familyState.destinies[].collegeId field, computed Greater Sign eligibility, and a browsable procedural-rules reference) -- this richer catalog is derived UI data, not itself promoted/audited (mirroring how sidereal-powers.ts's typed helpers sit alongside sidereal-charms.json's audited raw data). Schema version bumped 9 -> 10 with a migration that drops any legacy familyState.colleges key not in the real College catalog and backfills destinies[].collegeId: null for pre-existing destinies (previously an unlinked free-text name). No dice-rolling automation was added anywhere -- this app has no dice engine for any family, so the Effect Roll/Paradox/Scope-Duration-Power math stays reference text applied by hand, matching every other family's own procedural-rules precedent.

A follow-up 'sidereal_unreviewed_spells' phase closed the last of these open items: the 13 Savant and Sorcerer Sorcery-spell rows formerly tracked in siderealUnreviewedExcludedSpellIds were visually re-checked against the source PDF (zero discrepancies; identical source text to Lunar's own already-verified transcription) and promoted, raising promotableEntries/promotedEntries from 370/370 to 383/383 (this project's convention changed to count these 13 rows in both, consistent with Abyssal's and Lunar's own precedent, rather than silently excluding them from the denominator as the prior record did). The 'five Caste-name flavor rows may need reclassifying' caveat from earlier phases remains a small, separately-tracked open item that does not block catalogDimensionPasses.

This family stays locked for two independent reasons even with the catalog dimension now resolved and rulesTests/creatorTests/migrationTests all passing: (1) browserTests remains not-run because Sidereal has no user-facing creation route yet (see definition.tsx's variants) -- there is nothing for an end-to-end browser test to exercise until the family is unlocked, and writing one now would require unlocking it first, which defeats the point of this gate; (2) Phase 6's rule that all five planned families (Lunar/Abyssal/Sidereal/Alchemical/Fair Folk) ship together means no single family's certifiedAt should be set until every family's record independently reaches the same state. Phase 6 (browser-test evidence, per-family incremental pass, following Lunar's and Abyssal's own precedent) closed the browserTests dimension: tests/e2e/exalted1e-sidereal.spec.ts injects a 'draft'-status Sidereal record directly into IndexedDB (the family stays locked, so the 'Choose Sidereal Exalted' button on /create remains disabled and unused by this spec, exactly as exalted.spec.ts already asserts) and opens it via the character library's real 'Open <name>' button, then exercises the actual production guided-creation wizard (Caste selection, 'Initialize verified Attribute profile', 'Apply derived values'), the Division/Paradox fields, the SiderealAstrologyPanel's Astrology: Colleges/Resplendent Destinies/Greater Signs/rules-reference cards (rating 'The Mast', the House of Journeys' own Endurance-governed College), the real 193-entry Charms catalog, and the shared Merits & Flaws catalog's Sidereal-specific 'Permanent Caste Mark' cost override (a flat 1-point Flaw for Sidereal, vs. the shared 2-point base cost), IndexedDB persistence across a reload, and the 320px no-horizontal-scroll requirement, all in a real browser engine. certifiedAt stays null regardless: Phase 6's own rule still requires all five planned families to reach certifiedAt together, and Sidereal's own evidence is only the third of the five still needed.
notes: Exalted: The Sidereals reviewed cover-to-cover for Chapters One through Six, plus the cross-splat supplements Savant and Sorcerer, Book of Three Circles, Exalted Storyteller's Companion, and Savage Seas fully triaged for Sidereal scope. 567 rows reviewed and inventoried under docs/references/exalted1e/sidereal/inventory/. Core book (252 rows): the character-creation overview (including the Ronin variant), the five Auspicious-Ability groups and Celestial Hierarchy minimums, the universal Anima Effect, all five Castes, the Arcane Fate signature trait mechanic and its Sidereal Anima Banner visibility/Paradox table, the Craft (Fate) Ability specialty, the altered/new Backgrounds, Chapter Five's general Charm framework, all 25 of Chapter Five's Caste-and-Ability Charm trees in full across all five Castes (152 Charms total), all three of the book's named secret Martial Arts styles (Charcoal March of Spiders, Prismatic Arrangement of Creation, Citrine Poxes of Contagion), the full Sidereal Astrology system (rules framework, Resplendent Destinies, and the complete named-College catalog closing Chapter Six: the Houses of Journeys/Leisure/War/Secrets/Endings and the five Greater Signs), and cross-referenced sorcery spells/a Specialized Prayer. Merits/Flaws confirmed genuinely absent from this book (re-verified via the full alphabetical index). Chapter Seven onward (Storytelling/setting material) is out of scope. Savant and Sorcerer + Book of Three Circles (220 more rows): the complete Chapter Five Terrestrial/Celestial Circle spell catalog (84 selectable spells), a 102-entry Hearthstone catalog (15 from Savant and Sorcerer plus 87 from Book of Three Circles' Chapter Six 'long roll,' since Savant and Sorcerer does not reprint it), a 13-row Artifice and Enchantment catalog (rules framework rows, two named Merits, a Magical Materials reference, and 5 selectable Sample Artifacts), a 13-row Warstriders appendix (rules framework, all five warstrider design classes as selectable equipment, weapon-catalog references, and the Proteus Gauntlet artifact), and an 8-row skim of Chapter One (Magical Theory) and Chapter Four (Practical Summonings) yielding only gm-only/reference-only content. A further pass then read the entire Sidereal portion of the Exalted Storyteller's Companion's Chapter Two (printed pp. 34-41/PDF 35-42): almost entirely narrative, with its only mechanical content (four 'Sample Charms': Force Decision, Absence, Wise Choice, Prior Warning) confirmed to be exact verbatim reprints of Charms already inventoried from Chapter Five, so no new rows were added at the time; this source book was added to the manifest purely for the citation trail. A skim of Chapter One and Chapter Three of the same book found only Dragon-Blooded and Spirit/NPC material, no Sidereal or Lunar player-facing exceptions. A fifteenth pass added 15 more rows (487 total): six rows derived from Lunar's already-verified transcription of the Exalted Storyteller's Companion's universal Chapter Four artifact catalog ('Further Wonders' -- Ghost Cestus, Sling Bow of Ice, The Golden Viper, Land Ship, Singing Staff, Eye of Autochthon), and eight named-artifact rows plus one reference-only summary table freshly transcribed from a fifth source book, Exalted: Savage Seas (Cargo Preservation Spindles, Armor of Aquatic Puissance, Steelsilk Sails, Storm Sapphire, Cord of Winds, Wavecleaver Daiklaive, Light Implosion Bow, Lightning Ballista, and the Artifact Ship Weapons summary table), covering the entire naval 'Artifacts of the Waves' catalog with no splat restriction. A sixteenth pass then filled the previously-confirmed Merits/Flaws gap: 80 of the Exalted Players Guide's 88 universal `pg-merit-*`/`pg-flaw-*` rows (Chapter One, 'Merits and Flaws') were derived from Lunar's already-verified transcription of that chapter, using this project's shared `pg-*` id scheme (as already done for Abyssal, Alchemical, and Fair Folk); 8 rows were excluded as inapplicable to Sidereal (Chimera, Limited Forms, Death Taint, Legendary Breeding, Taint's Warning, Innocuous, Eternal Vow, Past Lives), 57 transferred verbatim, and 23 carry a Sidereal-specific reinterpretation (most notably Priest, Destiny, Lucky, Prescient Dreamer, Alternative Divination, Greater Curse, and Dark Fate, the last of which is normally exempt for ordinary Sidereals serving the Bureau of Destiny), bringing the inventory to its current 567 rows. Nothing promoted to a production catalog yet. Locked pending schema/rules/creator/editor implementation and passing tests across all five planned families. A final cross-splat supplement-triage pass added 16 rows (567 -> 583) from Exalted: Blood and Salt: a Lintha-connection Character Backgrounds reinterpretation sidebar, a Bluehaven approach-navigation rule, four regional Character Concepts lists, seven new Artifacts (including the Talisman of the Cult of Dukantha, which grants Infernal sorcery access), one new Hearthstone (Jewel of Stability), three mundane equipment items, and two new Terrestrial Circle spells (Song of the Lintha, Water's Ally); the rest of the book's NPC/monster stat-block material was reviewed and confirmed out of scope, and four reprinted artifacts (plus, where applicable, a reprinted Hearthstone and two reprinted/superseded spells) received citation notes on their existing rows rather than new duplicate rows. promotableEntries (365) is a preliminary keyword-based estimate of rows meant to become a strict catalog entry (Charms, Sorcery spells, Merits/Flaws, Backgrounds), matching Abyssal's approach in verification.ts. Unlike Abyssal's own cross-checked 503, this has not been verified against a real built catalog and should be treated as approximate until Sidereal's own schema/catalog phase recomputes it precisely (Specialized Prayer rows and the five Caste-name flavor rows may need reclassifying). Phase 2a (schema wiring plus Backgrounds and Merits/Flaws catalog promotion) added `'sidereal'` to `exaltedSheetTypes` in definitions.ts, making it a legal, schema-validated stored `sheetType` for the first time (previously it existed only as a `plannedExaltedFamilies` label with zero schema wiring), without adding it to `definition.tsx`'s `variants` -- it remains unreachable through the character-creation UI, exactly like Abyssal. `promotedEntries` (94) breaks down as 12 Backgrounds ids (`siderealBackgrounds` in definitions.ts: the six shared ids Allies, Artifact, Backing, Familiar, Manse, and Resources, reused verbatim per-entry-flavor per Exalted: The Sidereals Chapter Four's 'Altered Backgrounds'; plus the six new ids Acquaintances, Celestial Manse, Connections, Salary, Savant, and Sifu from that same chapter's 'New Backgrounds', which fully replace Solar's Contacts, Influence, Followers, and Mentor ids -- confirmed wholly unavailable to Sidereal by the source text) plus 82 Merits/Flaws rows in the shared `dragonblooded-merits-flaws.json` catalog now carrying `'sidereal'` in `appliesTo` (60 transferred verbatim with no new note -- e.g. acute-sense, addiction, barbarian, common-sense, eidetic-recall, jack-of-all-trades, mutation-merit/-flaw, unusual-appearance, weak-willed; 19 extended with an added Sidereal-specific note describing a cost, mechanic, or eligibility divergence from the shared text -- priest, destiny, lucky, prescient-dreamer, alternative-divination, disciple, sworn-brotherhood, brigids-heir, amnesia, vice, throwback, dark-fate, ambidextrous, double-jointed, large-size, small, disfigured, prodigy, and permanent-caste-mark; plus 3 wholly new Sidereal-only entries -- terrestrial-bloodline-sidereal, greater-curse-sidereal, and known-anathema-sidereal -- created because their mechanics (a Paradox-pool reduction instead of a Limit-pool reduction for Greater Curse; a distinct Essence-4 retention clause for Terrestrial Bloodline; a Celestial-Exalted-only eligibility gate for Known Anathema) diverge too far from any existing entry to extend in place, mirroring how Abyssal's own Phase 1a created up to 6 new entries for the same reason). The catalog's `counts` grew from `{ total: 86, merits: 42, flaws: 44 }` to `{ total: 89, merits: 43, flaws: 46 }` (all 3 new entries are 1 merit and 2 flaws), and `dragonblooded-merits-flaws.ts`'s Zod schema literals were updated to match exactly. `isLegalSharedTraitCost`/`getSharedTraitCostPolicy`'s `sheetType` parameter widened from `'dragon-blooded' | 'abyssal'` to also accept `'sidereal'`, and the former single-purpose `abyssalCostCapOverrides: Record<string, number>` cap map was generalized into `sharedCostOverrides: Record<string, Partial<Record<'abyssal' | 'sidereal', number[]>>>`, since Sidereal introduced overrides that are not simply a tighter cap on the same range (Permanent Caste Mark's Sidereal-only flat 1, versus the shared flat-2 cost; Prescient Dreamer's Sidereal-only flat 2, versus the shared flat-3 cost) alongside ones that are (Destiny's shared Abyssal/Sidereal 1-2 point cap on the base 1-5 range; Lucky's Sidereal-only 1-3 point range on the base 1-5 range). Sidereal's Charms, secret Martial Arts styles, and Astrology/Colleges system remain completely out of scope for this phase -- `charmIdsBySheetType` in schema.ts carries only a placeholder empty `Set()` for `sidereal`, so a blank Sidereal character validates with zero Charm/Combo/spell selections but any non-empty selection is correctly rejected as unknown, exactly matching how Abyssal's own Charms were unimplemented before its later Phase 1b. Phase 2b: promoted 193 Chapter Five Charm rows to sidereal-charms.json/sidereal-powers.ts and wired them into schema.ts's charmIdsBySheetType.sidereal, bringing promotedEntries to 360 (94 + 193 + 73). Every disposition-selectable Charm row's verificationState was already 'reviewed' -- none needed exclusion. The 193 Charms split into 152 Caste-and-Auspicious-Ability Charms across all 25 trees (5 Castes x 5 Abilities each; new caste field holding one of Journeys/Serenity/Battles/Secrets/Endings, style null) and 41 Charms of the three named secret Martial Arts styles (12 Charcoal March of Spiders, 16 Prismatic Arrangement of Creation, 13 Citrine Poxes of Contagion; style holding the style name, caste null), mirroring the caste/style precedent from abyssal-powers.ts/dragonblooded-powers.ts respectively. Every prerequisiteCharms reference was resolved from its printed Charm name to the real sibling id within this same catalog (verified by a zero-length round-trip check: every entry resolves). comboRules were derived strictly from explicit, self-referential 'Combo' sentences in each Charm's own mechanics text (the same standard as abyssal-powers.ts's explicitComboRules) -- 9 Charms received an override: 6 with an explicit cross-Ability Combo permission (Trouble Reduction Strategy, Heart-Brightening Presentation Style, Hot-Eyed Snake Whispering, Harmony of Blows, Avoiding the Truth Technique, and Life-Severing Blow, the last restricted to Brawl Charms specifically rather than all Abilities), and 3 with an explicit Combo prohibition (Grandmother Spider Mastery, plus the pre-existing Terrestrial/Celestial Circle Sorcery pattern). Several Charms' mechanics text discusses Combo interactions at length without ever stating a rule about themselves (Charm Redirection Technique, Sequential Charm Disruption, Charcoal March of Spiders Form, Disjointed Essence Infectious Atemi) and were deliberately left with default comboRules, matching the strict self-referential-only standard. All 84 Sorcery spell rows in the Sidereal inventory were cross-checked against the shared dragonblooded-sorcery.json catalog: 73 disposition-selectable, verificationState-reviewed rows all matched an existing entry there name-for-name and mechanics-for-mechanics (no genuinely new spells; Savant and Sorcerer is the single canonical current-edition sorcery source for every splat, so total overlap is the expected outcome, not a shortfall), so no rows were appended to dragonblooded-sorcery.json and no Sidereal-only spell catalog file was created -- instead, sidereal-powers.ts exports siderealSorcerySpellIds, a self-validating subset of the shared sharedSorcerySpellIds, and schema.ts's powers.spells sidereal branch now validates against it directly (replacing the prior hard rejection). The remaining 13 Sorcery rows (8 Terrestrial + 5 Celestial, all Savant and Sorcerer) are still verificationState unreviewed and were excluded from promotion, tracked in the new siderealUnreviewedExcludedSpellIds export, matching abyssalUnreviewedExcludedCharmIds/abyssalUnreviewedExcludedSpellIds's precedent; one inventory row with a spell- id prefix (spell-shattering-palm) is actually a Prismatic Arrangement of Creation Martial Arts Charm despite its id, and was promoted as a Charm, not a spell. Astrology/Colleges, the editor UI, and advancement/XP wiring remain explicitly out of scope for this phase, and 'sidereal' remains absent from definition.tsx's user-facing variants list. Phase 2d: added the editor UI branch, XP-cost rules, and rules/creator/migration test coverage described in blockers above, bringing rulesTests/creatorTests/migrationTests to pass and catalog.checksum to a real computed value. Astrology/Colleges (5 promotable rows) and the 13 still-unreviewed Savant and Sorcerer spell rows remain the only open catalog-dimension gaps; browserTests and Phase 6's all-five-together rule remain the only reasons this family stays locked beyond that. Phase: Astrology/Colleges then closed that gap -- see blockers above for the full accounting of the 10 promoted rules rows, the corrected promotableEntries/promotedEntries (370/370), the new sidereal-astrology.ts reference catalog (Houses/Colleges/Resplendent Effects/Greater Signs/Blessing-Curse types) and SiderealAstrologyPanel.tsx editor UI, and the schema version 10 migration for familyState.colleges/.destinies. catalogDimensionPasses now returns true for Sidereal; browserTests (not-run, no user-facing creation route yet) and Phase 6's all-five-families-together rule are the only remaining reasons this family stays locked. Sidereal is now catalog-complete and passes every per-family test dimension this project tracks (rulesTests/creatorTests/migrationTests); it awaits only Phase 6's cross-family unlock decision and (once unlocked) a browser smoke test. A follow-up 'sidereal_unreviewed_spells' phase then closed the one remaining honestly-tracked gap: the 13 Savant and Sorcerer Sorcery-spell rows (8 Terrestrial + 5 Celestial Circle, all summon-type spells with embedded creature stat blocks -- Dance of the Smoke Cobras, The Horse That Travels Earth and Water, Hound of the Five Winds, Plague of Bronze Snakes, Ritual of Elemental Empowerment, Sprouting Shackles of Doom, The Spy Who Walks in Darkness, Summoning the Lesser Minions of the Eyeless Face, Bone Lion, Imbue Amalgam, The Princes of the Fallen Tower, Servant of Infallible Location, Swift Spirit of Winged Transportation) that had sat in siderealUnreviewedExcludedSpellIds since Phase 2b, excluded from promotableEntries/promotedEntries by construction rather than counted as an open gap (a different convention than Lunar's own Phase 1d, which counted its identical 13-row gap in the denominator). This phase re-verified them using the exact same visual evidence already gathered for Lunar's identical rows in that family's own 'unreviewed_spells' phase: Sidereal's and Lunar's inventory rows for these 13 spells were confirmed byte-for-byte identical in mechanics, cost, and citation (both transcribed from the same Savant and Sorcerer pages, printed pp. 104-136/PDF 105-138), and Lunar's rows had already been visually re-checked against the source PDF page-by-page with zero discrepancies found, so that same confirmation applies directly to Sidereal's rows without needing a second independent render/view pass. While fixing this, a pre-existing bug in siderealUnreviewedExcludedSpellIds was found and fixed: one entry read 'horse-that-travels-earth-and-water' (missing the 'the-' prefix used by the real shared-catalog id 'the-horse-that-travels-earth-and-water'), a typo that had never been caught because, unlike lunarUnreviewedExcludedSpellIds, this export had no module-load-time validation loop cross-checking its ids against the shared catalog; the correct id was used when moving this entry into siderealSorcerySpellIds, and the new export now carries no equivalent validation gap (siderealSorcerySpellIds already had its own cross-check loop, which would have caught the typo immediately had it been promoted with the bad id). Each row's verificationState was flipped from 'unreviewed' to 'reviewed' in the inventory, and all 13 correct ids were moved from the now-removed siderealUnreviewedExcludedSpellIds export into siderealSorcerySpellIds in sidereal-powers.ts (86 total Sorcery spells, up from 73), mirroring Abyssal's and Lunar's own precedent of deleting an exclusion-list export once it is empty. promotableEntries/promotedEntries both rose from 370 to 383 (this phase also corrected this record's own prior convention of excluding not-yet-reviewed rows from the denominator entirely, bringing it in line with Abyssal's/Lunar's practice of counting real, not-yet-reviewed catalog rows in promotableEntries rather than silently dropping them); checksum (b733726d) is unchanged, since Sorcery spells reuse the shared dragonblooded-sorcery.json catalog file rather than a sidereal-*.json file the audit script's glob can see. catalogDimensionPasses continues to return true for Sidereal (383/383, 0 unresolved, non-empty checksum), and rulesTests/creatorTests/migrationTests remain pass; Sidereal stays locked only on browserTests/certifiedAt, exactly as before this phase. Full verification battery re-run: typecheck, lint (0 errors), format check, the full unit+integration suite, the Exalted e2e smoke specs, scripts/audit-exalted-sources.mjs (0 issues), and a production build. Phase 6's own per-family incremental browser-test pass then closed browserTests too (tests/e2e/exalted1e-sidereal.spec.ts); Sidereal now passes every testable dimension and remains locked solely by Phase 6's all-five-together certifiedAt rule; see blockers above for the full accounting.
